query:
site: nodes.GeneratingTasks.analyse_meeting_transcript
returns: list[MeetingTask]
tools: none

system:     This is a task you must complete by returning only the output.
    Do not include explanations, code, or extra text—only the result.
    
system: Task: Extract every concrete action item from the meeting transcript. Return only a JSON list of MeetingTask objects. Every object must contain exactly two non-empty string fields: name and description; never return an empty or placeholder task. Keep distinct commitments for different deliverables or owners as separate tasks. Combine discussion steps that belong to the same deliverable into one task, including approval followed by execution, rather than over-splitting them. Return an empty list only when the transcript contains no action items. Document owners, deadlines, requirements, and acceptance criteria stated in the transcript without inventing facts.

Inputs:
transcript (str): The complete meeting transcript from which to extract action items

Returns: list[MeetingTask]

Respond with a single JSON object.
Schema requirements:
- schema_object_wrapper (array)
user: self = GeneratingTasks()
transcript = 'Nadia: Okay, product sync. Three things on the agenda: the performance complaints, the dark mode request, and the database question Raj raised. Let's start with dark mode since it keeps coming up in reviews.

Raj: It's our second most requested feature. I sketched what it would take: theme tokens everywhere, new asset variants, QA across both themes. Roughly three weeks of work.

Nadia: Three weeks is a lot right now. Let's say we commit to it: Raj builds the theme system, Tom does the asset variants.

Tom: Actually, hold on. Before we commit to that, the design-system upgrade we already scheduled for September ships with theming built in. Tokens, dark palette, the lot. If we build our own now we'll throw it away in a month.

Raj: ...that's a good point. I forgot theming was in scope for that upgrade.

Nadia: Okay, scratch what I just said. We are not building dark mode this cycle. It comes for free with the September design-system upgrade, so no task there, and if anyone asks, that's the answer. Next: performance.

Raj: The dashboard is slow for accounts with lots of projects. I profiled it: 80% of the time is waiting on the database, and it's connection contention, not query cost. Which brings me to my database question. I was going to propose we evaluate moving to MongoDB.

Tom: We looked at Mongo eighteen months ago, the migration cost was brutal and half our reporting depends on SQL joins.

Nadia: Agreed. Let's settle it now: we're staying on Postgres, no migration, no evaluation task, I don't want that on the board. But the contention is real, so Raj, take a proper look at connection pooling instead. Benchmark PgBouncer in transaction mode against our current setup, with the dashboard workload, and bring numbers next sync.

Raj: Will do. I'll set up a load test that mirrors the dashboard's query pattern and compare p95 latency with and without PgBouncer.

Nadia: Perfect. Two small ones to finish. Marketing spotted a typo in the onboarding email, it says "recieve" in the subject line, of all places. Tom, just fix it and get it re-approved, five-minute job.

Tom: On it. I'll push the fix through the email template repo today.

Nadia: And the roadmap doc still shows dark mode under "Q3 committed", which after today is wrong. Tom, while you're in there, update the roadmap: move dark mode under the September design-system upgrade line so sales stops promising it as standalone.

Tom: Got it, I'll update the doc right after this.

Nadia: That's everything. Short and productive, my favorite kind.
'
